length_confound_removed.metric: AUROC obtainable from document length alone

significance.verdict: UNDERPOWERED. The 40% relative reduction rests on 9 misses versus 15. This validation split cannot resolve a difference this size.

caveat: AUROC 0.99997 on both arms means the validation split is saturated: the detector is scoring text from the same four generator families it trained on. The discriminating test is held-out generators (RAID, MAGE, HC3), which has not run.

superseded.status: SUPERSEDED for the arm result, still valid for the length-confound measurement
superseded.why: Every number in `result` was measured on dataset v0.1-min, whose AI half was generated without a chat template: the four instruction-tuned families in the roster were prompted as base models, so a third of generations came back empty and the survivors were continuations rather than answers. The corpus was regenerated as v0.2-min and both arms retrained. The current in-distribution result is in indist_baseline.json and indist_mirror.json; the out-of-distribution comparison, which is the one that answers the research question, is in ood_*.json with paired bootstraps in ood_significance_*.json and the matched-budget test in ood_mcnemar.json.
superseded.what_is_still_valid: `length_confound_removed` measures how much AUROC is obtainable from document length alone, and the chat-template defect does not change what that experiment measured on the corpus it ran against. It has NOT been re-measured on v0.2-min.
superseded.to_supersede_this_file: scripts/length_gate.py, re-run against the v0.2-min corpus
